title: Comparison of 1 Versus 2 Doses of Quadrivalent Influenza Vaccine in 3-8-Year-Old Children with Different Immunological States - Jiangsu Province, China, 2021.
ehr_evidence: In this open-label, self-paired clinical trial conducted in Donghai County, Jiangsu Province, China (ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT05313893), we enrolled healthy children aged 3–8 years.
summary: An open-label, self-paired clinical trial comparing one versus two doses of quadrivalent influenza vaccine in 252 healthy children aged 3-8 years, assessing immunogenicity (GMT, GMFI, SCR, SPR) and safety by prior vaccination/serostatus.
key_findings: In Group A (2+ prior doses), the second dose produced a slight decrease in antibody titers against H1N1 (0.92-fold, 95% CI: 0.85, 0.99) and BV (0.86-fold, 95% CI: 0.80, 0.93) versus the first dose, with no significant differences in SCR and SPR except a slight increase in SCR for BY strains after the second dose (P=0.039).

In Group B (vaccine-naive), the second dose increased SCR and SPR for H3N2, BY, and BV versus the first dose (P<0.001), with GMFIs of 1.48 (95% CI: 1.04, 1.31) for H1N1, 2.15 (95% CI: 1.74, 2.66) for BY, and 1.57 (95% CI: 1.33, 1.84) for BV.
Baseline serostatus significantly impacted antibody titers against all four strains; seropositive individuals consistently exhibited higher HI GMTs than seronegative individuals.
Overall adverse reaction incidence was 38.8% (50/129) in Group A and 22.5% (29/123) in Group B, with adverse reactions mainly grade 1-2 and no serious adverse events reported.
population: 252 healthy children aged 3-8 years in Donghai County, Jiangsu Province, China
limitations: Durability/persistence of immune responses over time was not investigated.
data_availability_statement: Supplementary data to this article can be found online.
